newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich support no surprise to White House aide.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich support no surprise to White House aide.

text.p: White House Chief of Staff Staff Leon Panetta predicted on Monday House Speaker Newt Gingrich would be reelected but said the Georgia Republican would be weakened by his admitted ethics violations.

"We all expected he'd have a pretty good chance of being reelected," Panetta said on the CNN Program "Larry King Live" in the first public comments from the White House on the controversy over Gingrich's speakership.
"We were not totally surprised," Pannetta said after Republicans emerged from a 3 1/2-hour meeting to declare solid support for the embattled speaker.
But the "bigger decision" lay ahead after Tuesday's vote, he added, referring to the House vote later this month on a punishment recommended by the Ethics Committee.
"Then the members have to make a very serious judgment ... each member has to make this judgment based on looking at the evidence. It is too serious not to be based on the evidence," Panetta said.

Asked if the ethics issue would weaken Gingrich, Panetta replied: "I don't think there's any question that obviously this will impact on the speaker -- assuming that he is reelected and stays in that job -- it's going to have some impact in the terms of his ability to continue to lead the House."
